note: The furthest outside the stated ICP of any call in this batch, and it closed. He is 24, a tattoo artist who has not worked for a year, carrying roughly $30,000 in unpaid ambulance bills from a $1.5m hospital episode and funding the purchase by selling cryptocurrency — 'successful' and 'makes good money' both fail outright. Health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise good life, it is an acute unresolved crisis eleven months after brain surgery, which is the explicit inverse of the 'neglected, not a crisis' test. And this is rescue in the most literal sense available — 'I just want to get back to my normal life and functioning normal again' — not good going to great. The single criterion he meets is the exclusion as literally worded: he is not fifty pounds overweight and gym-averse, he trains five days a week at home. That is precisely the finding. The stated ICP's only physical screen asks whether someone is overweight and unwilling, so it passes a man who cannot run, jump or crouch to tie his shoe, and it contains nothing that would stop a sale to someone with active post-surgical neurological symptoms. This call belongs alongside the Robyn Stillwater assessment in the ICP file as evidence that the buying population and the stated ICP have come apart — except here the gap is clinical rather than demographic.
